title: Theorem A
body_md: Let $k$ be any field, $G$ a finite group and $A\le G$ abelian with $\operatorname{char}k\nmid|A|$. For $\rho_A(d):=\min\{\operatorname{rk} B:B\le A,\ [A:B]\le d\}$ we have $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\ge\rho_A([F':K]_s)$ for every finite extension $F'/K$; in particular $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge\rho_A(d)$.

title: Theorem B
body_md: Let $\operatorname{char}k=0$, $p$ an odd prime, $\zeta$ a primitive $p$-th root of unity, $c=\zeta+\zeta^{-1}$ and $m=[k(\zeta):k]$. Then $\lceil m/2\rceil\le d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(\mathbb{Z}/p))\le[k(c):k]$; if $m$ is even the bounds meet, $d_1=m/2$. In particular $d_{1,\mathbb{Q}}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(\mathbb{Z}/p))=(p-1)/2$.

title: Theorem C
body_md: Let $\operatorname{char}k=0$. Then $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(S_5))=2$ for $d\le3$, $=1$ for $4\le d\le119$ and $=0$ for $d\ge120$. In particular $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(S_5))=4$.

label: fact:rs
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:rs}
Let $X$ be a $G$-variety, $\tau\colon T\to\operatorname{Spec} F$ a $G$-torsor. $X$ is \emph{$\tau$-weakly versal} if there is a $G$-equivariant morphism $T\to X_F$ over $F$, and \emph{$\tau$-versal} if every dense $G$-invariant open subvariety is $\tau$-weakly versal.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $X$ is $\tau$-weakly versal iff ${}^{\tau}\!X(F)\ne\emptyset$. More precisely ${}^{\tau}\!X(F)=\operatorname{Hom}_G(T,X_F)=\operatorname{Hom}_G^k(T,X)$.
\item If $X$ is smooth and $F$ is large, $X$ is weakly $\tau$-versal iff $X$ is $\tau$-versal.
\item If $X$ is generically free and primitive and $\tau$-versal, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(X)\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$.
\end{enumerate}
A field $F$ is \emph{large} if every irreducible $F$-variety with a smooth $F$-point has dense $F$-points; $F((t))$, henselian nontrivially valued fields, and $q$-closed fields are large \cite[\S7]{RS22}, \cite{Pop96,Pop14}.

label: lem:freepoint
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:freepoint}
Let $Z$ be a quasi-projective generically free primitive $G$-variety over $k$ and $\tau$ a $G$-torsor over $F$. If ${}^{\tau}\!Z$ has a free $F$-point, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\le\dim Z$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$G$ acts freely on the quasi-projective variety $Z^{\mathrm{free}}$, so the quotient $\pi\colon Z^{\mathrm{free}}\to B:=Z^{\mathrm{free}}/G$ exists and is a $G$-torsor \cite[Exp.~V, \S\S1--2]{SGA1}.
A free $F$-point is a $G$-equivariant $f\colon T\to Z^{\mathrm{free}}$; it induces $\bar f\colon\operatorname{Spec} F\to B$ with $f^*(\pi)\cong\tau$ (a $G$-equivariant map of torsors over $\operatorname{Spec} F$ is an isomorphism). If $b$ is the image point of $\bar f$, then $\tau$ is the base change of the torsor $\pi^{-1}(b)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ along $\kappa(b)\subseteq F$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(b)\le\dim B=\dim Z$.

label: prop:shape
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:shape}
Let $\tau$ be a $G$-torsor over $F\supseteq k$ and $H=\operatorname{im}\varphi_\tau$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $d\mapsto\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)$ is non-increasing with values in $\{0,\dots,\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\}$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}_k(\tau)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$, and $d_{\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)}=1\le d_{\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)-1}\le\dots\le d_0\le|H|$.
\item If $F'/F$ is a field extension of degree $e$ and $d\ge1$, then $\operatorname{ed}^{[de]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)$; hence $d_j(\tau)\le[F':F]\,d_j(\tau\otimes F')$ for every finite $F'/F$ and every $j$.
\item $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)=\min\{j:d_j(\tau)\le d\}$: the jump degrees determine the profile.
\item If $k\subseteq k'\subseteq F$ then $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_{k'}(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)$ for all $d$, with equality if $k'/k$ is algebraic.
\item $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)=0$ iff some $F'/F$ of degree $\le d$ makes $\tau\otimes F'$ descend to the algebraic closure of $k$ in $F'$; for $k$ algebraically closed, iff $\tau$ is split by an extension of degree $\le d$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: shape

title: Proof
body_md: (a) Over the splitting field $E$, $[E:F]=|H|$, the torsor is split, so $d_0\le|H|$; the rest is clear from the definition and (B1). (b) The first inequality: an extension $F''/F'$ of degree $\le d$ has $[F'':F]\le de$. The second: if $[F_1:F]\le d$ then the compositum $F_1F'$ (any composite field) has $[F_1F':F']\le d$ and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F_1F')\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F_1)$. If $[F'':F']=d_j(\tau\otimes F')$ realises $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F'')\le j$ then $[F'':F]=[F':F]\,d_j(\tau\otimes F')$. (c) is a restatement, (d) is (B2) applied to each $\tau\otimes F'$, (e) is (B3).

label: prop:d0
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:d0}
Let $H=\operatorname{im}\varphi_\tau$ and $E$ the splitting field of $\tau$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $d_0(\tau)\le\min\{[F':F]:\tau\otimes F'\text{ split}\}=|H|$, with equality if $k$ is algebraically closed.
\item Let $k$ be perfect and $E/k$ regular. If $[F':F]<\infty$ and $\tau\otimes F'$ descends to the algebraic closure $k_1$ of $k$ in $F'$, then $[k_1:k]\le[F':F]$ is finite and $[F':F]\ge|H|\cdot[k_1:k]$. In particular $d_0(\tau)=|H|$.
\item For $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ over a perfect $k$: $d_0(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=|G|$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')=0$ forces $[F':K]\ge|G|\,[k_1:k]$.
\end{enumerate}

name: the last jump degree

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) $T\otimes_FF'$ is split iff $E$ embeds $F$-linearly into $F'$, which forces $[F':F]\ge|H|$; $F'=E$ works; for $k$ algebraically closed use (B3).
(b) First, $[k_1:k]\le[F':F]$: as $F\subseteq E$ and $E/k$ is regular, $k$ is algebraically closed in $F$, so for every finite $k'/k$ inside $k_1$ the ring $k'\otimes_kF$ is a field, equal to $k'F\subseteq F'$, of degree $[k':k]$ over $F$. Now let $\tau\otimes F'\cong\tau_0\otimes_{k_1}F'$ with $\tau_0$ over $k_1$, of splitting field $l/k_1$ Galois with group $H_0$. The total spaces of $\tau\otimes F'$ and $\tau_0\otimes_{k_1}F'$ are isomorphic $F'$-algebras, each a product of copies of one field, namely a compositum $EF'$ (for some $F$-embedding of $E$ into a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $F'$), respectively $lF'$ (for some $k_1$-embedding of $l$). An $F'$-isomorphism $EF'\to lF'$ extends to an $F'$-automorphism of $\Omega$; it fixes $k_1\subseteq F'$, so after replacing $l$ by its image we may assume $EF'=lF'$. Since $l/k$ is finite separable and $E/k$ regular, $l\otimes_kE$ is a field and $[lE:E]=[l:k]=|H_0|[k_1:k]$; as $lE\subseteq EF'$,
\[
|H_0|[k_1:k]\,|H|=[lE:E][E:F]\le[EF':F]=[lF':F'][F':F]\le|H_0|\,[F':F].
\]
(c) $E=L$ is regular over $k$ and $H=G$.

label: lem:pi
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pi}
Let $\operatorname{char}k=p$, $k$ perfect, $G$ any finite group, and $F'/F$ finite purely inseparable. Then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes_FF')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$. Consequently $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)$ is the minimum over separable $F'/F$ of degree $\le d$.
head: environment
name: purely inseparable invariance

title: Proof
body_md: Choose $m$ with $F'\subseteq F^{1/p^m}$ (inside an algebraic closure). Then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$, and it suffices to prove $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m})\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$. Let $\sigma\colon F^{1/p^m}\to F$, $x\mapsto x^{p^m}$; it is a field isomorphism with $\sigma(k)=k$ since $k$ is perfect. For any $G$-torsor $\tau'$ over $F^{1/p^m}$ let $\sigma_*\tau'$ be the torsor over $F$ obtained by transport of structure. The map $F_0\mapsto\sigma(F_0)$ is a bijection between subfields of $F^{1/p^m}$ containing $k$ and subfields of $F$ containing $k$, preserving $\operatorname{trdeg}_k$, and $\tau'$ descends to $F_0$ iff $\sigma_*\tau'$ descends to $\sigma(F_0)$; so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\sigma_*\tau')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau')$. Finally $\sigma_*(\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m})\cong\tau$: the $p^m$-power map extends to $F^{1/p^m}F^{\rm sep}\to F^{\rm sep}$ and commutes with all automorphisms, so the induced isomorphism $\Gamma_{F^{1/p^m}}\to\Gamma_F$ is the canonical one (restriction along $F\subseteq F^{1/p^m}$, an isomorphism of absolute Galois groups), and the classifying homomorphism of $\sigma_*(\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m})$ is $\varphi_\tau$. The last statement: any finite $F'/F$ is purely inseparable over its separable closure $F'_s$ in $F'$, $[F'_s:F]\le[F':F]$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F'_s)$.

label: lem:ind
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ind}
For finite groups $H\le G$ and an $H$-torsor $\tau_H$ over $F$, $\operatorname{ed}_k(\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_H)$.
head: environment
name: induced torsors

title: Proof
body_md:
``$\le$'': if $\tau_H$ is defined over $F_0\subseteq F$ by an $H$-torsor $\tau_0$, then $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_0$ is a $G$-torsor over $F_0$ that becomes $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H$ over $F$.

``$\ge$''. Step 1: we may assume $T_H$ is a field. Write $T_H$ for the total space of $\tau_H$; it is a product of fields permuted transitively by $H$, so $\tau_H=\operatorname{Ind}_{H'}^H\tau'$ with $\tau'$ an $H'$-torsor whose total space $T'$ is a field. Then $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H=\operatorname{Ind}_{H'}^G\tau'$ and, by ``$\le$'', $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_H)\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau')$; so it suffices to show $\operatorname{ed}_k(\operatorname{Ind}_{H'}^G\tau')\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau')$.

Step 2: a descent of $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H$ and its stabiliser. Let $T_0\to\operatorname{Spec} F_0$ be a $G$-torsor, $F_0\subseteq F$, with $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=\operatorname{ed}_k(\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H)$ and $T_0\otimes_{F_0}F\cong\operatorname{Ind}_H^G T_H$. Let $T_0'$ be a connected component of $T_0$, a field, with stabiliser $H_0\le G$. The components of $T_0'\otimes_{F_0}F$ are among the $gT_H$ (the components of $\operatorname{Ind}_H^GT_H$) and are permuted transitively by $H_0$. After replacing $H$ by a conjugate $gHg^{-1}$ and $T_H$ by $gT_H$ (which does not change $\operatorname{Ind}_H^GT_H$ up to isomorphism) we may therefore assume $T_H\subseteq T_0'\otimes_{F_0}F$ is one of them, and then $H\le H_0$, since $H$ stabilises $T_H$.

Step 3: $\tau_H$ descends to $F_1:=(T_0')^H$. The extension $F_1/F_0$ is separable ($T_0'$ is \'etale over $F_0$), so $F_1\otimes_{F_0}F=\prod_iF_i$ is a product of fields. The factor $T_0'\otimes_{F_1}F_{i_0}$ through which $T_H$ factors is an $H$-torsor over $F_{i_0}$ whose total space is a product of fields permuted transitively by $H$; $T_H$ is $H$-stable and is one of these components, so $T_H$ is that factor. Now $F_{i_0}$ is an $F$-algebra through the second factor of $F_1\otimes_{F_0}F$, so $F\subseteq F_{i_0}$; and $F_{i_0}\subseteq T_H$ is fixed by $H$ (which acts $F_1$-linearly, $F_1=(T_0')^H$), so $F_{i_0}\subseteq T_H^H=F$. Hence $F_{i_0}=F$. Thus $\tau_H$ is defined over $F_1\subseteq T_0'$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_1=\operatorname{trdeg}_kT_0'=\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0$, because $T_0'/F_1$ is finite. Hence $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_H)\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H)$.

label: prop:bfe
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:bfe}
Let $k'/k$ be finite of degree $d$. Then $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(G)$. More precisely, every field factor $F'$ of $F\otimes_kk'$ has $[F':F]\le d$ and

\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')=\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(\tau\otimes F')\le\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(G),

with equality on the left because $k'/k$ is algebraic.

title: Proof

label: cor:rou
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:rou}
Let $e$ be the exponent of $G$, $\operatorname{char}k\nmid e$, and $d_e=[k(\mu_e):k]$. For every $G$-torsor $\tau$ over every $F\supseteq k$,
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[d_e]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[[F(\mu_e):F]]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_e)}(G).
\]
In particular: (i) if $G$ is abelian, $\operatorname{ed}^{[d_e]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{rk} G$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer} over $k(\mu_e)$); (ii) if $G$ is a $p$-group and $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[p-1]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[[k(\mu_p):k]]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[[F(\mu_p):F]]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_p)}(G)$, the minimal dimension of a faithful representation of $G$ over $k(\mu_p)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:KM}).

name: roots-of-unity defect

title: Proof
body_md: Proposition~\ref{prop:bfe} with $k'=k(\mu_e)$ (resp.\ $k'=k(\mu_p)$ in (ii)): $F(\mu_e)$ is a field factor of $F\otimes_kk(\mu_e)$, of degree $[F(\mu_e):F]\le d_e$ over $F$, so $\operatorname{ed}^{[[F(\mu_e):F]]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F(\mu_e))\le\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_e)}(G)$, and the middle inequality is monotonicity. The values in (i), (ii) are Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer} and Theorem~\ref{thm:KM}.

label: rem:rou
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:rou}
For $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ and $F'=K(\mu_e)=Kk(\mu_e)$ the torsor $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F'$ is the generic torsor of $V$ over $k(\mu_e)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:regular}(c), proved in Section~\ref{sec:sylow}), so Proposition~\ref{prop:bfe} gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K(\mu_e))=\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_e)}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K(\mu_e))=\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_e)}(G)$: the bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:rou} for $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is realised by the extension $K(\mu_e)$. It is not optimal in general. Corollary~\ref{cor:rou} is the case $k'=k(\mu_e)$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:bfe}, and for $G=\mathbb{Z}/p$, $p$ odd, the smaller field $k'=k(\zeta_p+\zeta_p^{-1})$ already gives $\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(\mathbb{Z}/p)\le1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:B1}, proved in Section~\ref{sec:thmB}); this halves the degree whenever $\zeta_p\notin k(\zeta_p+\zeta_p^{-1})$. Exactly when Corollary~\ref{cor:rou} is sharp for $\mathbb{Z}/p$ in characteristic $0$ is determined in Corollary~\ref{cor:sharp}, with one family of cases left open.

name: geometric meaning of the profile

title: Proof
body_md:
(2)$\Leftrightarrow$(3): a closed point $x$ of ${}^{\tau}\!Z$ with residue field $F'=\kappa(x)$ is an $F'$-point of ${}^{\tau}\!Z\otimes_FF'={}^{\tau\otimes F'}\!Z$, free iff $x$ lies in the open free locus (which commutes with base change); conversely the image of $\operatorname{Spec} F'\to{}^{\tau\otimes F'}\!Z\to{}^{\tau}\!Z$ is a point with residue field contained in $F'$, hence finite over $F$, hence closed, of degree $\le[F':F]$, and free if the $F'$-point is. The identification of free $F'$-points with equivariant maps $T_{F'}\to Z^{\mathrm{free}}$ is Fact~\ref{fact:rs}(a).

(3)$\Rightarrow$(1): Lemma~\ref{lem:freepoint} gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le\dim Z\le m$.

(1)$\Rightarrow$(3): let $[F':F]\le d$ and $\tau\otimes F'\cong\tau_0\otimes_{F_0}F'$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0\le m$. Replacing $F_0$ by the subfield generated over $k$ by the finitely many coefficients that define $\tau_0$ and the isomorphism $\tau\otimes F'\cong\tau_0\otimes_{F_0}F'$, we may assume $F_0$ finitely generated over $k$. Spread $\tau_0$ out to a $G$-torsor $Z\to B$ over an integral affine $k$-variety $B$ with $k(B)=F_0$, $\dim B\le m$. Then $Z$ is quasi-projective, $G$ acts freely (so $Z^{\mathrm{free}}=Z$) and $Z$ is primitive (its generic fibre $T_0$ is a torsor over the field $F_0$, on whose components $G$ acts transitively). The composite $T_{F'}\to T_0\to Z$ is $G$-equivariant.

For $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$: $F'$ is a finite extension of $K=k(V/G)$, so it is the function field of a variety $B'$ with a finite dominant map $B'\to V/G$ of degree $[F':K]$, and $W':=$ normalisation of $V\times_{V/G}B'$ is a $G$-variety (action on the first factor) with $k(W')=L\otimes_KF'$ (a product of fields) and $W'\to V$ dominant of degree $[F':K]$. An equivariant $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_KF')\to Z^{\mathrm{free}}$ is an equivariant rational map $W'\dashrightarrow Z^{\mathrm{free}}$. If $L\otimes_KF'$ is a field, $T_{F'}$ is connected, hence so is $T_0$, so $\tau_0$ is a field and $Z$ is irreducible with faithful action.

The ingredients are: the existence of the twist ${}^{\tau}\!Z=(T\times_kZ)/G$ as a quasi-projective $F$-scheme compatible with base change and open immersions \cite[\S3]{DR15}; the identification of $F$-points of ${}^{\tau}\!Z$ with equivariant maps $T\to Z_F$ (elementary for finite $G$); the fact that $Z^{\mathrm{free}}\to Z^{\mathrm{free}}/G$ is a $G$-torsor \cite[Exp.~V, \S\S1--2]{SGA1}; and spreading out. None of these depends on the characteristic or on $G$.

title: Remark

\label{rem:rs101}
Theorem~10.1 of \cite{RS22} says: for generically free primitive $G$-varieties $X$, $Y$ with $X$ smooth, a $G$-equivariant correspondence $Y\rightsquigarrow X$ of degree prime to $q$ gives $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(X)\ge\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(Y)$; the proof passes through the $q$-closure, which is large, and Fact~\ref{fact:rs}(b). The prime-to-$q$ part of the profile is thus governed by \cite[Thm.~10.1]{RS22} (Theorem~\ref{thm:div}); the $q$-power part is not.

label: lem:qcl
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:qcl}
Let $q$ be a prime, $S\le\Gamma_F$ a Sylow pro-$q$ subgroup and $F^{(q)}=(F^{\rm sep})^S$. Then $F^{(q)}$ is a union of finite subextensions of degree prime to $q$, every finite separable extension of $F^{(q)}$ has $q$-power degree, and $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(\tau)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F^{(q)})$ \cite[(2.5)]{RS22}. If $F'/F$ is finite separable with $q\nmid[F':F]$, then there is an $F$-embedding $F'\hookrightarrow F^{(q)}$, and hence $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\ge\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(\tau)$.

name: $q$-closure

title: Proof
body_md: The first three statements are quoted. $F'\otimes_FF^{(q)}$ is a product of finite separable extensions of $F^{(q)}$, each of $q$-power degree, whose degrees sum to $[F':F]$; if none had degree $1$ the sum would be divisible by $q$. So some factor is $F^{(q)}$, giving the embedding, and (B1) gives the inequality. (For a given embedding $F'\subseteq F^{\rm sep}$ the compositum $F'F^{(q)}$ need not be $F^{(q)}$: $F=\mathbb{Q}$, $q=2$, $F'=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]2)$ has $F'\otimes_\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{Q}^{(2)}\cong\mathbb{Q}^{(2)}\times\mathbb{Q}^{(2)}(\sqrt{-3})$.)

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:qinv}
Let $q$ be a prime and $k'/k$ a finite separable extension with $q\nmid[k':k]$. Then $\operatorname{ed}_{k',q}(G)=\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)$ (compare \cite[Prop.~2.4]{Mer13}, which has the corresponding statement for ed at a prime under base change; we give the short proof for completeness).

name: prime-to-$q$ extensions of the base field

title: Proof
body_md:
For a $G$-torsor $	au$ over a field $F\supseteq k'$, $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(	au)$ and $\operatorname{ed}_{k',q}(	au)$ are minima over the same set of extensions $F'/F$ of $\operatorname{ed}_k(	au\otimes F')$ and $\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(	au\otimes F')$, which agree by (B2) since $k'/k$ is algebraic; so $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(	au)=\operatorname{ed}_{k',q}(	au)$, and taking suprema, $\operatorname{ed}_{k',q}(G)\le\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)$. Conversely let $	au$ be a $G$-torsor over a field $F\supseteq k$. The algebra $F\otimes_kk'$ is 'etale of dimension $[k':k]$, so it has a field factor $F_1$ with $q
mid[F_1:F]$; $F_1/F$ is separable and $F_1\supseteq k'$. Every finite separable $F''/F_1$ with $q
mid[F'':F_1]$ is finite separable over $F$ with $q

label: thm:div
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:div}
Let $k$ be perfect (for instance of characteristic $0$). Let $\tau$ be a $G$-torsor over $F$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item For every prime $q$ and every $j<\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(\tau)$, $q$ divides $d_j(\tau)$: every $F'/F$ with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le j$ has $q\mid[F':F]$.
\item Every prime $q$ with $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)>j$ divides $d_j(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})$; hence $d_j(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge\prod_{q:\,\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)>j}q$.
\item For every $d\ge1$,
$\displaystyle\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ \ge\ \min_{1\le d'\le d}\ \max_{q\nmid d'}\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)\ \ge\ \max_{q>d}\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)$ ($q$ prime).
\item The prime-to-$q$ profile $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k{}'(\tau)=\min\{\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F'):[F':F]\le d,\ q\nmid[F':F]\}$ is non-increasing with terminal value $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(\tau)$, reached at a finite prime-to-$q$ degree; for $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ the terminal value is $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof

label: lem:regular
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:regular}
Let $V$ be a faithful representation of $G$ over $k$, $L=k(V)$, $K=L^G$, all inside an algebraically closed field $\Omega$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $K/k$ is regular.
\item For every algebraic extension $k'/k$ inside $\Omega$, $K\otimes_kk'$ is a field, so $[Kk':K]=[k':k]$ when $k'/k$ is finite; and $Kk'=k'(V)^G$.
\item $L\otimes_KKk'\cong Lk'=k'(V)$ as $G$-algebras. Hence $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KKk'$ is the generic torsor of $V_{k'}$ over $k'$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: $K$ is regular over $k$; base change of $\tgen$

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) $L=k(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ is purely transcendental, hence regular over $k$; subextensions of regular extensions are regular \cite[VIII~\S4]{La}.

(b) A regular extension is linearly disjoint from every algebraic extension \cite[VIII, Thm.~4.12]{La}, so $K\otimes_kk'$ is a field, of degree $[k':k]$ over $K$ when this is finite. For the second claim: $Lk'$ is generated by $k'$ and the $x_i$, which remain algebraically independent over $k'$ for transcendence-degree reasons, so $Lk'=k'(V)$. Since $G$ acts $k'$-linearly, $Kk'\subseteq(Lk')^G$. Now $Lk'=L\cdot Kk'$ gives $[Lk':Kk']\le[L:K]=|G|$, while $[Lk':(Lk')^G]=|G|$ by Artin's theorem. Hence $Kk'=(Lk')^G$.

(c) The natural map $L\otimes_KKk'\to Lk'$ is surjective and $G$-equivariant, and both sides have dimension $|G|$ over $Kk'$.

label: thm:KM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:KM}
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and $k$ a field with $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$ containing a primitive $p$-th root of unity. Then
\[
\operatorname{ed}_k(G)=\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(G)=\operatorname{rdim}_k(G).
\]
head: environment
name: Karpenko--Merkurjev

label: prop:KMplateau
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:KMplateau}
Let $G$ be a $p$-group, $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$ ($k$ perfect if positive), and $c=[k(\mu_p):k]$, a divisor of $p-1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item For $c\le d\le p-1$: $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\operatorname{rdim}_{k(\mu_p)}(G)=\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(G)$; the profile is constant on $[c,p-1]$.
\item For $1\le d<c$: $\operatorname{rdim}_{k(\mu_p)}(G)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(G)$, with equality on the right for $d=1$.
\item If $\zeta_p\in k$: $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\operatorname{rdim}_k(G)=\operatorname{ed}_k(G)$ for $1\le d\le p-1$, and every drop of the profile occurs at a multiple of $p$: $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\operatorname{ed}^{[p\lfloor d/p\rfloor]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})$ for $d\ge p$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: the Karpenko--Merkurjev plateau

title: Proof
body_md: This is Proposition~\ref{prop:qgp}(a),(b),(d) with $q=p$, in which $\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_p)}(G)=\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_p),p}(G)=\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(G)$ is rewritten as $\operatorname{rdim}_{k(\mu_p)}(G)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:KM} over $k(\mu_p)$. Explicitly: every degree $\le p-1$ is prime to $p$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:div}(c) gives the lower bound $\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(G)$ for all $d\le p-1$; Corollary~\ref{cor:rou}(ii) gives $\operatorname{ed}^{[c]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_{k(\mu_p)}(G)$; and the two values agree by Theorem~\ref{thm:KM} over $k(\mu_p)$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:qinv} applied to the separable extension $k(\mu_p)/k$ of degree $c$ prime to $p$. (c) is (a) with $c=1$ together with Proposition~\ref{prop:qgp}(c).

label: rem:KMscope
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:KMscope}
The lower bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:KM} is a bound on the canonical $p$-dimension of the classifying variety, and canonical $p$-dimension is insensitive to correspondences of degree prime to $p$; in the language of Theorem~\ref{thm:geom} and Remark~\ref{rem:rs101}, the Karpenko--Merkurjev theorem controls exactly the Sylow-governed, prime-to-$p$ part of the profile, which is the plateau of Proposition~\ref{prop:KMplateau}. The $p$-power part, beginning with $\operatorname{ed}^{[p]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})$, is beyond the method: a correspondence of degree $p$ can lower the canonical $p$-dimension. In (b), the profile can drop below $\operatorname{ed}_k(G)$ before degree $c$: for $G=\mathbb{Z}/p$ in characteristic $0$ with $c$ even and $c\ge4$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[c/2]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=1<2\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p)$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:sharp}(ii)).

label: prop:subrdim
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:subrdim}
For every subgroup $H\le G$ and every field $k$,
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[[G:H]]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(H)\le\operatorname{rdim}_k(H).
\]
If $G$ is a $p$-group, $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$ and $\zeta_p\in k$, then for every $j\ge0$
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ \le\ r_j(G,k):=\min\{\operatorname{rdim}_k(H):H\le G,\ [G:H]\le p^j\},
\]
and $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(H)=\operatorname{rdim}_k(H)$ is realised by the fixed field $L^H$ of any $H$ of index $\le p^j$.

name: subgroup bound

title: Proof
body_md: The first chain is Corollary~\ref{cor:sub} and $\operatorname{ed}_k(H)\le\operatorname{rdim}_k(H)$. For the second, $[G:H]$ is a power of $p$, at most $p^j$, so Corollary~\ref{cor:sub} and monotonicity give $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(H)$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(H)=\operatorname{rdim}_k(H)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:KM} applied to the $p$-group $H$.

label: ex:rdim
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:rdim}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$, $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$. For every such $k$, $\operatorname{rdim}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=[k(\zeta_{p^n}):k]$: a faithful representation has an irreducible summand on which the generator has order exactly $p^n$, and the irreducible representations with this property are the irreducible factors of $\Phi_{p^n}$ over $k$, all of dimension $[k(\zeta_{p^n}):k]$. For $\zeta_p\in k$ we have $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=[k(\zeta_{p^n}):k]$: this is the case $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:KM}; Florence \cite{Fl08} proved it earlier under further conditions on the roots of unity in $k$. Now let $\zeta_p\in k$ and $[k(\zeta_{p^n}):k]=p^{n-1}$ (e.g.\ $k=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ for $p$ odd, or $k=\mathbb{Q}$ for $p=2$); then every step of the tower $k\subset k(\zeta_{p^2})\subset\dots\subset k(\zeta_{p^n})$ has degree $p$, and
\[
\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=\operatorname{rdim}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=p^{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le p^{\,n-1-j}\quad(0\le j\le n-1),
\]
the bound being realised in two ways of the same degree $p^j$: by the fixed field $L^H$ of the index-$p^j$ subgroup $H=\langle g^{p^j}\rangle\cong\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j}$, for which $\operatorname{rdim}_k(H)=[k(\zeta_{p^{n-j}}):k]=p^{n-1-j}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:subrdim}), and by adjoining $\zeta_{p^{j+1}}$: $k'=k(\zeta_{p^{j+1}})$ has $[k':k]=p^j$ and $\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=[k'(\zeta_{p^n}):k']=p^{n-1-j}$, so Proposition~\ref{prop:bfe} gives the same bound. By Proposition~\ref{prop:KMplateau}(c) the profile is constant $=p^{n-1}$ on $[1,p-1]$ and drops only at multiples of $p$: a staircase $p^{n-1},p^{n-2},\dots,1,0$ at the degrees $1,p,\dots,p^{n-1},p^n$ is consistent with everything known, and $d_0=p^n$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:d0}(c). For cyclic $G$ the rank--index theorem gives nothing beyond $d_0$ (Remark~\ref{rem:limits}).
\end{enumerate}

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:constant}
\textup{(i)} Let $G$ be a finite group, $\tau$ a $G$-torsor over an infinite field $F\supseteq k$, and $t$ transcendental over $F$. Then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes_FF(t))=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$. \textup{(ii)} Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $F$ (for instance an elliptic curve, or the Jacobian of a curve), or more generally a proper $F$-variety such that $A_{\bar F}$ is isomorphic to an abelian variety, and let $F'=F(t_1,\dots,t_m)$ be purely transcendental. name: purely transcendental base change

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) $\le$ is \cite[Lemma~2.1(a)]{RS22}. Conversely let $\tau\otimes F(t)\cong\tau_0\otimes_{F_0}F(t)$ with $F_0\subseteq F(t)$, $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=e$; replacing $F_0$ by the subfield generated over $k$ by the finitely many coefficients of equations defining $\tau_0$, we may assume $F_0$ finitely generated. Spread $\tau_0$ out to a $G$-torsor $Z\to B_0$ over an integral $k$-variety $B_0$ with $k(B_0)=F_0$, $\dim B_0=e$. The inclusion $F_0\subseteq F(t)$ is a dominant rational map $\mathbb{A}^1_F\dashrightarrow B_0$, defined on a dense open $U$, and the isomorphism of torsors over $F(t)$ spreads out to an isomorphism between the pullback of $Z$ and the constant torsor $\tau\times U'$ over a dense open $U'\subseteq U$. Since $F$ is infinite, $U'$ has an $F$-point $c$; restricting to $c$, $\tau$ is the pullback of $Z$ along $\operatorname{Spec} F\to B_0$, whose image point $b$ has $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(b)\le e$. Hence $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\le e$.

(ii) By induction on $m$ (replacing $F$ by $F(t_1,\dots,t_{m-1})$) it suffices to treat $m=1$. A point of $A(F(t))$ is a rational map $\mathbb{P}^1_F\dashrightarrow A$, which extends to a morphism $\phi\colon\mathbb{P}^1_F\to A$ since $A$ is proper and $\mathbb{P}^1_F$ is a regular curve. The base change $\phi_{\bar F}\colon\mathbb{P}^1_{\bar F}\to A_{\bar F}$ is constant: otherwise its image would be a rational curve on the abelian variety $A_{\bar F}$, and an abelian variety contains no rational curves \cite[Ch.~I, Prop.~3.9]{Mil}.
Hence $\phi(\mathbb{P}^1_F)$ is a single point $a$. As $\mathbb{P}^1_F$ is reduced, $\phi$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(a)$, and an $F$-morphism $\mathbb{P}^1_F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(a)$ is an $F$-algebra map $\kappa(a)\to H^0(\mathbb{P}^1_F,\mathcal O)=F$; so $\kappa(a)=F$ and $\phi$ is the constant map to the $F$-point $a$.

title: Proof

The stabiliser $H_0\supseteq H$ of $i_0$ acts faithfully on the field $P^{(i_0)}$, which is finite over $E$. title: Proof

A $k$-embedding $\varphi:M\to\Omega$ is an $\Omega$-point $x_\varphi$ of $C$ lying over the generic point. Put $\mathcal D=\sum_ix_{\varepsilon_i\iota}$, an effective divisor of degree $e$ on $C_\Omega$.

The class is constant. Let $J=\operatorname{Pic}^0_C$, $P_0\in C(k)$, $\alpha:C\to J$, $x\mapsto[x-P_0]$, and $\beta=\sum_i\alpha(x_{\varepsilon_i\iota})\in J(\Omega)$. Since $N_0/L$ is separable, the $\varepsilon_i$ are the $e$ distinct $L$-embeddings, $\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega/L)$ permutes them, and $\mathcal D$ is the base change to $\Omega$ of an $L$-rational effective divisor on $C_L$ (the image of the closed point $\operatorname{Spec} N_0\to C_L$, with multiplicity $[N_0:L\cdot M]$); so $\beta\in J(L)$. As $L$ is purely transcendental over $k$ (and $J=0$ if $g(C)=0$), $J(L)=J(k)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:constant}(ii). Hence $\beta=c\in J(k)$, and $[\mathcal D]=c+eP_0$ is the class of a $k$-rational divisor $D$; thus $\mathcal D\in|D|(\Omega)$.

(a). Since $N_0/L$ is separable, $\mathcal D$ is the base change to $\Omega$ of the effective $L$-rational divisor on $C_L$ obtained from the closed point $\operatorname{Spec} N_0\to C_L$ (with multiplicity $[N_0:L\cdot M]$), so it is an $L$-point of $|D|\cong\mathbb{P}^r_k$. If $r=0$, $|D|$ is a single divisor $D_0$ over $k$, whose support lies over closed points of $C$; but each $x_{\varepsilon_i\iota}$ lies over the generic point. So $r\ge1$.

(b). Let $g\in G$ and choose $\gamma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega/k)$ with $\gamma|_L=g|_L$. Then $\varepsilon_i'=\gamma\varepsilon_ig^{-1}$ is an $L$-embedding, $i\mapsto i'$ is a bijection, and $\gamma\varepsilon_i\iota=\varepsilon'_i\iota\,g|_M$. On generic-type points $\gamma(x_\varphi)=x_{\gamma\varphi}$ and $h_g(x_\varphi)=x_{\varphi\circ g|_M}$, so $\gamma(\mathcal D)=h_g(\mathcal D)$. Since $\gamma$ fixes $k$ and $D$ and preserves linear equivalence, $h_g(\mathcal D)=\gamma(\mathcal D)\sim D$; also $h_g(\mathcal D)\sim h_g(D)$. Hence $h_g(D)\sim D$.

name: tame structure

title: Proof
body_md:
Step 1: reduction to the henselisation. If $\nu|_E$ is trivial then $r=0$, $E=\kappa(E)$ is algebraically closed, $E^s=E$ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise let $Z\subseteq E^s$ be the fixed field of $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E$. Then $(Z,\nu|_Z)$ is a henselisation of $(E,\nu|_E)$ \cite[\S5.2]{EP}; it is an immediate extension, so $\nu(Z^\times)=\nu(E^\times)=:\Delta_E$ and $\kappa(Z)=\kappa(E)$ \cite[\S5.2]{EP}; and $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E=\operatorname{Gal}(E^s/Z)$. (If $\sigma\in\mathrm{Dec}_E$ then $\nu|_{E^s}\circ\sigma|_{E^s}=\nu|_{E^s}$, so $\rho_E(\mathrm{Dec}_E)\subseteq\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E$.)

Step 2: inertia and ramification. $\kappa(E^s)$ is algebraic over the algebraically closed field $\kappa(Z)=\kappa(E)$, so the two are equal, and the inertia group of $\nu|_{E^s}$ over $Z$ is all of $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E$ (inertia equals decomposition because the residue field is algebraically closed; this is what lets us apply the description of inertia modulo ramification below to $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E$). Let $R\trianglelefteq \overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E$ be the ramification group; it is a pro-$\varepsilon$ group (trivial if $\varepsilon=1$), and, with $\Delta:=\nu((E^s)^\times)$,
\[
\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E/R\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta/\Delta_E,\kappa(E)^\times)
\]
as profinite groups, the standard description of tame inertia over a henselian field \cite[Thm.~5.3.3]{EP}.
Moreover $\Delta/\Delta_E$ is torsion because $E^s/E$ is algebraic \cite[Cor.~3.2.3]{EP}, i.e.\ $\Delta\subseteq\Delta_E\otimes\mathbb{Q}$. Hence every homomorphism $\Delta/\Delta_E\to\kappa(E)^\times$ takes values in the group $\mu_\infty(\kappa(E))$ of roots of unity of $\kappa(E)$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta/\Delta_E,\kappa(E)^\times)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta/\Delta_E,\mu_\infty(\kappa(E)))$.

Step 3: removing the $\varepsilon$-part. Put $P:=\bar\psi(R)$ and $Q:=\bar\psi(\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E)$. As $\bar\psi$ is continuous and $G$ is finite, $P$ is a finite quotient of the pro-$\varepsilon$ group $R$, hence an $\varepsilon$-group, and it is normal in $Q$ because $R\trianglelefteq \overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E$. Since $|B|$ is prime to $\varepsilon$, $B\cap P=1$, so $B$ embeds in $Q/P$, and $\bar\psi$ induces a continuous surjection $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E/R\to Q/P$.

Step 4: finite continuous quotients of $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E/R$ have rank $\le r$. Let $X:=\Delta/\Delta_E$, a discrete torsion group, and $X'$ its prime-to-$\varepsilon$ part. As $\kappa(E)$ is algebraically closed of characteristic exponent $\varepsilon$, $\mu_\infty(\kappa(E))$ is isomorphic to the prime-to-$\varepsilon$ part of $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$; so $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E/R\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X',\mu_\infty(\kappa(E)))$ is the Pontryagin dual of $X'$. A finite continuous quotient of the dual of the discrete torsion group $X'$ is the dual $\hat S$ of a finite subgroup $S\subseteq X'$ (an open subgroup $U$ of the dual is the annihilator of the finite subgroup $S=U^\perp$, and the quotient by $U$ is $\hat S$), and $\hat S\cong S$. For each prime $\ell$, inside $\Delta_E\otimes\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
S[\ell]\subseteq X[\ell]\subseteq(\ell^{-1}\Delta_E)/\Delta_E\cong\Delta_E/\ell\Delta_E,
\]
the last isomorphism being multiplication by $\ell$ ($\Delta_E$ is torsion-free). Finally $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_\ell}\Delta_E/\ell\Delta_E\le r$: given $r+1$ elements $\gamma_i$ of $\Delta_E$ there is a relation $\sum n_i\gamma_i=0$ with integers $n_i$ not all zero, and dividing by their greatest common divisor (using that $\Delta_E$ is torsion-free) we may assume $\gcd(n_i)=1$, so some $n_i\not\equiv0\pmod\ell$. Hence $\operatorname{rk} S=\max_\ell\dim_{\mathbb{F}_\ell}S[\ell]\le r$.

Step 5. $Q/P$ is a finite continuous quotient of $\overline{\mathrm{Dec}}_E/R$, hence abelian of rank $\le r$, and $B$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $Q/P$; so $\operatorname{rk} B\le r$.

title: Proof
body_md:

name: Kummer

title: Proof
body_md:
By the invariant-factor decomposition, $B\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathbb{Z}/e_i$ with $1<e_1\mid e_2\mid\dots\mid e_r\mid e$; here $r=\operatorname{rk} B$, since $B$ is generated by $r$ elements and $B/\ell B\cong\mathbb{F}_\ell^r$ for a prime $\ell\mid e_1$. Fix isomorphisms $\mathbb{Z}/e_i\cong\mu_{e_i}\subset k^\times$. For a field $F\supseteq k$, Kummer theory gives $H^1(F,\mathbb{Z}/e_i)\cong H^1(F,\mu_{e_i})\cong F^\times/F^{\times e_i}$, and $H^1(F,B)=\prod_iH^1(F,\mathbb{Z}/e_i)$. So every $B$-torsor over $F$ is
\[
\textstyle\bigotimes_{F,i}F[t_i]/(t_i^{e_i}-a_i)\qquad(a_i\in F^\times),
\]
the tensor product over $F$ of the Kummer algebras (of dimension $\prod_ie_i=|B|$), with $\mathbb{Z}/e_i$ acting on $t_i$ through $\mu_{e_i}$. It is the base change of the $B$-torsor $\bigotimes_{E_0,i}E_0[t_i]/(t_i^{e_i}-a_i)$ over $E_0:=k(a_1,\dots,a_r)$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_kE_0\le r$.

body_md: A subgroup $B\le(\mathbb{Z}/q)^n$ is elementary abelian, so $|B|=q^{\operatorname{rk} B}$. Hence $\operatorname{rk} B\le j$ implies $[G:B]\ge q^{n-j}$, with equality for $B\cong(\mathbb{Z}/q)^j$; and for $1\le d\le q^n$, $[G:B]\le d$ implies $|B|\ge q^n/d$, so $\operatorname{rk} B\ge\lceil n-\log_qd\rceil=n-\lfloor\log_qd\rfloor$, with equality for $B\cong(\mathbb{Z}/q)^{n-\lfloor\log_qd\rfloor}$, whose index $q^{\lfloor\log_qd\rfloor}$ is $\le d$. Thus $\rho_G(d)=n-\lfloor\log_qd\rfloor$, and (a) is Theorem~\ref{thm:rankindex} with $A=G$. For (b), let $B\cong(\mathbb{Z}/q)^m\le G$. A $B$-torsor over $F\supseteq k$ is an $m$-tuple of $\mathbb{Z}/q$-torsors ($H^1(F,B)=H^1(F,\mathbb{Z}/q)^m$); each descends to a subfield of transcendence degree $\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/q)\le1$, and all of them to the compositum of these subfields, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(B)\le m$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:sub}, $\operatorname{ed}^{[q^{n-m}]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le m$; with $m=n-\lfloor\log_qd\rfloor$ and monotonicity this is the upper bound $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le n-\lfloor\log_qd\rfloor$, and with $m=0$ it gives $\operatorname{ed}^{[q^n]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=0$. Together with (a) this proves (b), and (c) is the case $q=2$.

body_md:
\label{rem:A8}

Corollary~\ref{cor:A8} also improves the case $G=(\mathbb{Z}/q)^n$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:d0}(c), which needs $k$ perfect: (a) gives $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge1$ for all $d<q^n$ over every $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\ne q$ (if $[G:B]\le d<q^n$ then $B\ne1$). label: cor:subgroupabelian
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:subgroupabelian}
Let $G$ be abelian of exponent $e$, $\operatorname{char}k\nmid e$, $\mu_e\subset k$. Then $\operatorname{rdim}_k(H)=\operatorname{rk} H$ for every $H\le G$, and
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\min\{\operatorname{rdim}_k(H):H\le G,\ [G:H]\le d\}\qquad\text{for all }d\ge1.
\]
In particular equality holds in \eqref{eq:subgroupformula} for every abelian $p$-group $G$ of exponent $p^a$ when $\mu_{p^a}\subset k$.
head: environment
name: the subgroup formula for abelian groups

title: Proof
body_md: Let $H\le G$. A representation of $H$ over $k$ is a direct sum of characters $H\to\mu_e\subset k^\times$, since the operators commute and are annihilated by $X^e-1$, which splits over $k$ with distinct roots. It is faithful iff the intersection of the kernels of its characters is trivial, iff these characters generate the character group $\hat H=\operatorname{Hom}(H,\mu_e)$ (by duality of finite abelian groups, a subgroup of $\hat H$ whose elements have trivial common kernel is all of $\hat H$). As $\mu_e$ is cyclic of order $e$ and the exponent of $H$ divides $e$, $\hat H\cong H$, so $\operatorname{rdim}_k(H)$ is the minimal number of generators of $\hat H$, namely $\operatorname{rk} H$. Now apply Corollary~\ref{cor:A7}.

label: rem:Z4Q
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Z4Q}
The hypothesis $\mu_e\subset k$ in Corollaries~\ref{cor:A7} and~\ref{cor:subgroupabelian} cannot be weakened to $\zeta_p\in k$, the hypothesis of the subgroup formula: for $G=\mathbb{Z}/4$ and $k=\mathbb{Q}$ (where $\zeta_2=-1\in k$) one has $\operatorname{rk} G=1$ but $\operatorname{ed}_\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{Z}/4)=\operatorname{rdim}_\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{Z}/4)=[\mathbb{Q}(i):\mathbb{Q}]=2$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:KM}, Example~\ref{ex:rdim}), so the rank formula of Corollary~\ref{cor:A7} fails at $d=1$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:rankindex} is not sharp there. The subgroup formula itself does hold for $\mathbb{Z}/4$ over $\mathbb{Q}$: the right side of \eqref{eq:subgroupformula} is $2,1,1,0$ for $d=1$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, $d\ge4$; and $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}_\mathbb{Q}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\operatorname{ed}_\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{Z}/4)=2$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_\mathbb{Q}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{Z}/2)=1$ for $d\in\{2,3\}$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:sub}) with equality by Proposition~\ref{prop:d0}(c), and $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_\mathbb{Q}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=0$ for $d\ge4$.

label: lem:cyclo
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cyclo}
Let $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$. Then $\operatorname{Gal}(k(\zeta)/k(c))=\Theta\cap\{\pm1\}$, and $-1\in \Theta$ iff $m$ is even. Hence: if $m$ is even, then $\zeta\notin k(c)$ and $[k(c):k]=m/2$; if $m$ is odd, then $k(c)=k(\zeta)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: $\zeta$ is a root of $T^2-cT+1$, so $[k(\zeta):k(c)]\le2$ and $\operatorname{Gal}(k(\zeta)/k(c))$ consists of the $a\in \Theta$ fixing $c$. Now $\zeta^a+\zeta^{-a}=\zeta+\zeta^{-1}$ iff $T^2-(\zeta^a+\zeta^{-a})T+1=T^2-cT+1$ iff $\{\zeta^a,\zeta^{-a}\}=\{\zeta,\zeta^{-1}\}$ iff $a=\pm1$. Since $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$ is cyclic, $-1$ is its unique element of order $2$, and the subgroup $\Theta$ of order $m$ contains it iff $m$ is even.

label: thm:Zp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Zp}
Let $\operatorname{char}k=0$. Then
\[
\Big\lceil\tfrac m2\Big\rceil\ \le\ d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ \le\ [k(c):k].
\]
If $m$ is even (equivalently $\zeta\notin k(c)$), the two bounds coincide: $d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=[k(c):k]=m/2$. In particular, over $k=\mathbb{Q}$, $d_{1,\mathbb{Q}}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(\mathbb{Z}/p))=(p-1)/2$.

name: the first jump degree of $\Z/p$

label: lem:B1
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:B1}
Let $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$ and $k':=k(c)$. Every $\mathbb{Z}/p$-torsor over a field $F\supseteq k'$ descends to a subfield $E$ with $k'\subseteq E\subseteq F$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_{k'}E\le1$. Hence $\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(\mathbb{Z}/p)\le1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Reductions. A split torsor descends to $k'$, and if $F$ is finite then $E=F$ will do. Otherwise, as $|G|=p$ is prime, the torsor is $\operatorname{Spec} M$ for a cyclic field extension $M/F$ of degree $p$ with $G=\operatorname{Gal}(M/F)$, and $F$ is infinite.

A rank-two representation. Let $W=k'^2$ with $\sigma$ acting by
\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&c\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det(T-S)=T^2-cT+1=(T-\zeta)(T-\zeta^{-1}).
\]
Since $p$ is odd, $\zeta\ne\zeta^{-1}$, so $S$ is diagonalisable over $k'(\zeta)$ with eigenvalues $\zeta^{\pm1}$, $S^p=1$ and $S\ne1$. Let $x_1,x_2\in W^*$ be the coordinate functions; $\sigma$ acts on $W^*$ (contragrediently) by $\sigma x_i=s_{i1}x_1+s_{i2}x_2$ for a matrix $(s_{ij})\in\mathrm{GL}_2(k')$, again diagonalisable with eigenvalues $\zeta^{\pm1}$. Let $\mu(u)=(s_{11}u+s_{12})/(s_{21}u+s_{22})$ be the corresponding M\"obius transformation of $\mathbb{P}^1(\bar k)$. Its fixed points are the eigenlines of $(s_{ij})$ written as $[u:1]$, so $\mu$ has exactly two fixed points $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{P}^1(k'(\zeta))$; one of them may be $\infty$.

Equivariant points. Let $U:=(W\otimes_{k'}M)^G$, with $G$ acting diagonally. By Galois descent for the $G$-Galois extension $M/F$, the natural map $U\otimes_FM\to W\otimes_{k'}M$ is an isomorphism; so $\dim_FU=2$ and $U$ spans $W\otimes_{k'}M$ over $M$. Each $w\in U$ defines a $k'$-algebra map $f_w\colon k'[W]=\operatorname{Sym}(W^*)\to M$ by $f_w(x)=\langle x,w\rangle$ for $x\in W^*$ (the $M$-linear extension of the evaluation pairing), and $f_w$ is $G$-equivariant because $w$ is $G$-invariant.

Avoiding the fixed points. Consider the $F$-linear maps $U\to M$ given by $w\mapsto f_w(x_2)$ and, for each fixed point $\gamma\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$ that is finite and lies in $M$, $w\mapsto f_w(x_1)-\gamma f_w(x_2)$. They are nonzero, because the $M$-linear forms $x_2$ and $x_1-\gamma x_2$ on $W\otimes_{k'}M$ are nonzero and $U$ spans $W\otimes_{k'}M$ over $M$. So their kernels are at most three proper $F$-subspaces of $U$, and since $F$ is infinite some $w\in U$ lies in none of them.

A small invariant subfield. Put $u=f_w(x_1)/f_w(x_2)\in M$; this is defined since $f_w(x_2)\ne0$. By equivariance,
\[
\sigma(u)=\frac{f_w(\sigma x_1)}{f_w(\sigma x_2)}=\frac{s_{11}u+s_{12}}{s_{21}u+s_{22}}=\mu(u).
\]
The point $u\in\mathbb{P}^1(\bar k)$ is not fixed by $\mu$: $u\ne\infty$; $u\ne\gamma$ for a finite fixed point $\gamma\in M$ by the choice of $w$; and $u\ne\gamma$ for a fixed point $\gamma\notin M$, as $u\in M$. So $\sigma(u)\ne u$. The field $M_1:=k'(u)\subseteq M$ is $G$-stable ($\mu$ has coefficients in $k'$), $G$ acts faithfully on it ($\sigma$ moves $u$ and $|G|$ is prime), and $\operatorname{trdeg}_{k'}M_1\le1$.

Descent. $E:=M_1^G\subseteq M^G=F$ contains $k'$, and $M_1/E$ is $G$-Galois (Artin). The $F$-algebra map $M_1\otimes_EF\to M$ is a $G$-equivariant morphism of $G$-torsors over $F$, hence an isomorphism. So the torsor descends to $E$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_{k'}E=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k'}M_1\le1$.

label: cor:pertorsor
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:pertorsor}
Let $\operatorname{char}k\ne p$. For every $\mathbb{Z}/p$-torsor $\tau$ over every field $F\supseteq k$,
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[[k(c):k]]}_k(\tau)\le1,\qquad\text{i.e. }\ d_{1,k}(\tau)\le[k(c):k]\ \text{ if }\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\ge1.
\]

name: the per-torsor bound

title: Proof
body_md: Let $F'$ be a field factor of $F\otimes_kk(c)$, so $[F':F]\le[k(c):k]$ and $F'\supseteq k(c)$. title: Proof

label: cor:sharp
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:sharp}
Let $\operatorname{char}k=0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $m=1$, then $d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=1=m$: Corollary~\ref{cor:rou} is sharp.
\item If $m\ge2$ and $-1\in \Theta$ (equivalently $m$ is even, equivalently $\zeta\notin k(c)$), then $d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=m/2$: Corollary~\ref{cor:rou} overshoots by exactly a factor $2$, and the optimum is attained by the constant-field extension $Kk(c)$.
\item If $m\ge2$ and $-1\notin \Theta$ (equivalently $m$ is odd and $m\ge3$; then $k(c)=k(\zeta)$), then $\frac{m+1}2\le d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le m$, and it is not known whether Corollary~\ref{cor:rou} is sharp (Question~\ref{q:sharpodd}).
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md: (i) $1\le d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le m$. (ii) Lemma~\ref{lem:cyclo} and Theorem~\ref{thm:Zp}, the witness being that of Corollary~\ref{cor:pertorsor}. title: Question
body_md:
\label{q:sharpodd}
Let $\operatorname{char}k=0$ and let $m=[k(\zeta_p):k]$ be odd, $m\ge3$. Is $d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(\mathbb{Z}/p))=m$? The smallest case is $p=7$, $k=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7})$: this is the quadratic subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)$ (as $7\equiv3\bmod4$), so $m=3$, and $d_{1,k}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\in\{2,3\}$.

label: rem:stalls
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:stalls}
For an extension $F'/K$ with $[F':K]=d$ that is not a constant-field extension, the argument gives a $G$-curve with at least $m$ fixed points (one Galois orbit, Step~5) and Riemann--Hurwitz and Castelnuovo give $r\le2d$ (Step~10), hence $d\ge m/2$, i.e.\ $d\ge(m+1)/2$ for $m$ odd. To exclude $m/2<d<m$ one would need either more fixed points than one Galois orbit, or a sharper genus bound than Castelnuovo's for curves whose function field is generated by functions of degree $\le d$ over a base of genus $g(D)$; we know of no way to obtain either from non-constant quadratic extensions. For instance, at $p=7$, $k=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7})$ ($m=3$) the method excludes $d=1$ but not $d=2$.

label: lem:S5curves
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:S5curves}
Let $k=\bar k$ have characteristic $0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $S_5$ acts faithfully on a smooth projective curve, every $A_5$-orbit has at least $12$ points.
\item Every homomorphism $S_5\to\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$ has kernel containing $A_5$.
\item $S_5$ has no faithful action on a curve of genus $0$ or $1$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: faithful $S_5$-curves

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) A point stabiliser acts faithfully on the cotangent line: in characteristic $0$, if a finite-order automorphism fixes $x$ and is trivial on $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$, averaging a uniformiser gives a fixed uniformiser, so it is the identity. Stabilisers are therefore cyclic; cyclic subgroups of $A_5$ have order $\le5$, so orbits have size $\ge60/5=12$.
(ii) The kernel is normal, so it is $1$, $A_5$ or $S_5$. If it were $1$, $S_5$ would be a subgroup of order $120$ of $\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$; the finite subgroups of $\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$ are cyclic, dihedral, $A_4$, $S_4$, $A_5$, so it would be dihedral of order $120$ and contain an element of order $60$, whereas elements of $S_5$ have order $\le6$.
(iii) Genus $0$ is (ii). For genus $1$, $\operatorname{Aut}(C)=C\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}(C,O)$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(C,O)$ cyclic, so a finite subgroup is an extension of a cyclic group by an abelian group, hence solvable.

label: prop:S5lower
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:S5lower}
Let $k=\bar k$ have characteristic $0$ and $[F':K]\le3$. Then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\ge2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le1$ and take $N_0,H$ as in Section~\ref{ss:tors}, so $[G:H]$ divides $[F':K]\le3$. $S_5$ has no subgroup of index $3$ (the action on three cosets would have kernel in $\{1,A_5,S_5\}$ and image of order $\le2$, which is not transitive); so $H=S_5$ or $H=A_5$; in particular $H\ne1$.

Case $H=A_5$. Then $[F':K]=2$ and $N_0=L$, so $F'\to L$ identifies $F'$ with the unique quadratic subfield $F_1=L^{A_5}$, and $\tau\otimes_KF_1=\operatorname{Ind}_{A_5}^{S_5}(L/F_1)$. Here $L/F_1$ is the generic $A_5$-torsor of $V|_{A_5}$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:ind} gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(L/F_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(A_5)\ge\operatorname{rk} V_4=2$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:rankindex} with $d=1$ and $A=V_4\le A_5$ (this is also the lower bound of Reichstein--Youssin \cite{RY}, so this case does not depend on the new theorem). Contradiction.

Case $H=G$. Then $N_0=L\otimes_KF'$ is a field of degree $e=[F':K]\in\{1,2,3\}$ over $L$. Proposition~\ref{prop:witness} gives a faithful $S_5$-curve $C$ and a $G_C$-invariant class $D$ of degree $e$ with $r=\dim|D|\ge1$.
If $r\ge2$: for special $D$, Clifford gives $2r\le e\le3$, impossible; so $D$ is non-special, $r=e-g(C)$ and $g(C)\le1$, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:S5curves}(iii).
If $r=1$ (here only (i) and (ii) of Lemma~\ref{lem:S5curves} are used, not the genus): $G_C$ acts on $|D|\cong\mathbb{P}^1$ by $E\mapsto h^*E$; this action is projective-linear because $h^*\mathcal O(D)\cong\mathcal O(D)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:S5curves}(ii) $A_5$ acts trivially, so every effective $E\in|D|$ is $A_5$-invariant; its support is a union of $A_5$-orbits, each of size $\ge12$, while $\deg E=e\le3$. Contradiction.

label: lem:edqSn
title: Lemma

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $m=\lfloor n/q\rfloor$; $S_n$ contains $(\mathbb{Z}/q)^m$, generated by $m$ disjoint $q$-cycles. (The result is also in \cite[Cor.~4.2]{MR09}.) For $H\le G$ and an $H$-torsor $\tau_H$ over $F$, $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G(\tau_H\otimes F')=(\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H)\otimes F'$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:ind} gives $\operatorname{ed}_k((\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\tau_H)\otimes F')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_H\otimes F')$ for all finite separable $F'/F$ of degree prime to $q$; hence $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(G)\ge\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(H)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:qinv} with $k'=k(\mu_q)$ (separable of degree dividing $q-1$) and Theorem~\ref{thm:KM} over $k'$, $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}((\mathbb{Z}/q)^m)=\operatorname{ed}_{k',q}((\mathbb{Z}/q)^m)=\operatorname{rdim}_{k'}((\mathbb{Z}/q)^m)=m$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Case $\sqrt5\in k$ (Klein). Then $A_5$ acts on the $k$-conic $Q$. Let $T_1=L/F_1$ be the $A_5$-torsor. The twist ${}^{T_1}Q$ is a conic over $F_1$; a rational line meets it in a subscheme of degree $2$ (it is a smooth conic in $\mathbb{P}^2$), so it has a point over a quadratic extension $F_2/F_1$ and ${}^{T_1}Q\cong\mathbb{P}^1_{F_2}$. The free locus is non-empty and open and $F_2$ is infinite, so it has an $F_2$-point. By Lemma~\ref{lem:S5free}, $\operatorname{ed}_k(T_1\otimes F_2)\le1$. As $\tau\otimes_KF_1=\prod_{S_5/A_5}L=\operatorname{Ind}_{A_5}^{S_5}T_1$, (T3) gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F_2)\le1$, and $[F_2:K]=4$. Here $K(\sqrt{5\Delta})=F_1$.

Case $\sqrt5\notin k$. Let $k'=k(\sqrt5)$ with generator $\sigma$ of $\operatorname{Gal}(k'/k)$.

Step 1: an $S_5$-action on a $k$-curve. Let $X=Q_{k'}$, viewed as a $k$-scheme; $X_{\bar k}=Q\sqcup Q^\sigma$. The two $3$-dimensional characters of $A_5$ are swapped both by $\sigma$ and by conjugation by a transposition $t$, so $\rho^\sigma\cong\rho\circ c_t$ over $k'$: there is $U\in\operatorname{GL}_3(k')$ with $\rho^\sigma(a)=U\rho(tat)U^{-1}$. Let $\mathsf S(x)=U^{-1}\sigma(x)$, a $\sigma$-semilinear automorphism of $\mathbb{P}^2_{k'}$ with $\mathsf S^{-1}(y)=\sigma(U)\sigma(y)$. Then
\[\mathsf S\rho(a)\mathsf S^{-1}=U^{-1}\rho^\sigma(a)U=\rho(tat).\]
Also $\mathsf S^2(x)=(\sigma(U)U)^{-1}x$, and applying $\sigma$ to the defining relation gives
\[\rho(a)=(\sigma(U)U)\rho(a)(\sigma(U)U)^{-1};\]
by absolute irreducibility $\sigma(U)U$ is a scalar, so $\mathsf S^2=\operatorname{id}$ on $\mathbb{P}^2$. The conic $\mathsf S(Q)$ is stable under $\rho(A_5)$ (use $\rho(a)\mathsf S=\mathsf S\rho(tat)$), so its equation is a semi-invariant quadratic form, hence invariant because $A_5$ is perfect, hence a multiple of $q$: $\mathsf S(Q)=Q$. The relations of $S_5=A_5\rtimes\langle t\rangle$ hold for $a\mapsto\rho(a)$, $t\mapsto\mathsf S$, so $S_5$ acts on $X$ by $k$-automorphisms; $A_5$ acts $k'$-linearly and odd elements $\sigma$-semilinearly. The action is faithful (a kernel meets $A_5$ trivially and is normal). Odd elements swap the two components of $X_{\bar k}$, so $X_{\mathrm{free}}$ is the complement of a finite set.

Step 2: the twist. Let $F_1^\flat=K(\sqrt{5\Delta})=K(\sqrt5\,\delta)$, quadratic over $K$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed in $L$, $\sqrt5\notin L$, so $N=L\otimes_KF_1^\flat=L(\sqrt5)$ is a field, $\operatorname{Gal}(N/K)=S_5\times\langle\sigma\rangle$, and $\operatorname{Gal}(N/F_1^\flat)=\{(g,\sigma^\epsilon):(-1)^\epsilon=\operatorname{sgn}g\}\cong S_5$, with $g(\sqrt5)=\operatorname{sgn}(g)\sqrt5$. This is the action of $G$ on $L\otimes_KF_1^\flat$ through the first factor, so $\tau\otimes_KF_1^\flat=\operatorname{Spec} N$ as $S_5$-torsors.
Now $X\times_kN=Q_{k'}\times_{k'}\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_kN)$ and $k'\otimes_kN\cong N\times N$, $a\otimes n\mapsto(an,\sigma(a)n)$. An element $g\in S_5$ acts on $k'\otimes N$ by $g|_{k'}\otimes g|_N$ with $g|_{k'}=\sigma^{[g\text{ odd}]}$; the first coordinate of the image of $a\otimes n$ is $\sigma(a)g(n)=g(a)g(n)=g(an)$ for odd $g$ (and $g(an)$ for even $g$), so $G$ preserves both components. The first component is $Q_N$, and the second is its $\sigma$-conjugate, which is again $Q_N$ since $q$ has coefficients in $k$. By descent ${}^NX=Y_1\sqcup Y_2$ with $Y_i$ smooth projective geometrically integral of genus $0$ over $F_1^\flat$, i.e.\ conics. The conic $Y_1$ is embedded in $\mathbb{P}^2_{F_1^\flat}$ by its anticanonical system, so a rational line cuts it in a subscheme of degree $2$, so there is a quadratic $F_2/F_1^\flat$ with $Y_1\cong\mathbb{P}^1_{F_2}$; it has an $F_2$-point in the non-empty open $Y_1\cap{}^N(X_{\mathrm{free}})$. This is a $G$-equivariant $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(N\otimes_{F_1^\flat}F_2)\to X_{\mathrm{free}}$, and $N\otimes_{F_1^\flat}F_2=\tau\otimes_KF_2$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:S5free}, $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F_2)\le1$, and $[F_2:K]=4$.

label: rem:strict
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:strict}
The profile can drop strictly below every subgroup bound and every base-field bound. Take $k=\bar k$ of characteristic $0$ and $G=S_5$. Over an algebraically closed field the finite groups of essential dimension $1$ are the cyclic groups and the dihedral groups of order $2m$ with $m$ odd \cite[Thm.~6.2]{BR97}. The largest such subgroup of $S_5$ is $D_5$, of order $10$, so the bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:sub} for $j=1$ is $[S_5:D_5]=12$, and there are no non-trivial constant-field extensions of $k$. But $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(S_5))=4$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:S5}): the optimal extension of degree $4$ is not a subgroup fixed field, since $\operatorname{ed}(A_5)=2$, and it is not a constant-field extension. It is a quadratic extension of the discriminant field $L^{A_5}$ that splits a twisted conic.

label: ex:Sn
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:Sn}
Let $\operatorname{char}k=0$, $L=k(x_1,\dots,x_n)$, $F=K=k(s_1,\dots,s_n)$, so $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is the generic degree-$n$ \'etale algebra. For $F_m=F(x_1,\dots,x_m)$, $[F_m:F]=n(n-1)\cdots(n-m+1)$, Corollary~\ref{cor:sub} gives
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[n(n-1)\cdots(n-m+1)]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F_m)=\operatorname{ed}_k(S_{n-m}),
\]
the equality being Lemma~\ref{lem:ind} applied to the generic $S_{n-m}$-torsor.
With $\operatorname{ed}_{k,q}(S_n)\ge\lfloor n/q\rfloor$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:edqSn}),
Theorem~\ref{thm:div} gives $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge\lfloor n/q_d\rfloor$ for the least prime $q_d>d$, so the profile of the generic \'etale algebra decays no faster than $\sim n/d$. For $S_6$, with $\operatorname{ed}_k(S_6)=3$, $\operatorname{ed}_k(S_5)=\operatorname{ed}_k(S_4)=2$, $\operatorname{ed}_k(S_3)=1$ (\cite[Thm.~6.5(d)]{BR97} for $S_4,S_5,S_6$; for $S_3$ the generic cubic reduces to $x^3+ax+a$):
$\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}_k=3$; $\operatorname{ed}^{[6]}_k\le2$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[120]}_k\le1$, $d_0=720$. Since $\operatorname{ed}_{k,2}(S_6)\ge3$ and $\operatorname{ed}_{k,3}(S_6)\ge2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:edqSn}), Theorem~\ref{thm:div} gives $2\mid d_2$ and $6\mid d_1$, hence $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k\ge2$ for $2\le d\le5$; so $d_2\in\{2,4,6\}$ and $d_1\in6\mathbb{Z}\cap[6,120]$. The discriminant field $L^{A_6}$, of degree $2$, is a witness for $d_2=2$ only if $\operatorname{ed}_k(A_6)\le2$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:sub} and Lemma~\ref{lem:ind}).

(c) What is $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}(A_5))$ over fields not containing $\sqrt5$? label: q:structure
title: Question
body_md:
\label{q:structure}
The upper bounds we use are subgroup fixed fields (Corollary~\ref{cor:sub}) and constant-field extensions (Proposition~\ref{prop:bfe}), which combine to $\operatorname{ed}^{[[k':k]\,[G:H]]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_{k'}(H)$. For which $(G,k)$ is the profile of $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ given by this combined bound? It is for abelian groups with enough roots of unity (Corollary~\ref{cor:subgroupabelian}) and is not for $S_5$ (Remark~\ref{rem:strict}). Is there a structural description of optimal extensions in general, for instance as a tower of subgroup fixed fields, constant-field extensions and splittings of twisted curves, as in Klein's reduction?
